title: Aftershock Sampling Runbook and Rollout Gating Walkthrough
content:
Purpose:
This runbook captures a pragmatic, testable approach for 'aftershock' sampling after a regional rollout and a gating walkthrough for safe ramping. It combines an operator checklist, a compact rollout calendar, and a release-notes draft block to be copied into customer comms. Use this for medium-risk platform releases (serving-runtime, routing, or batching changes).

Goals:
- Protect global SLOs while enabling predictable capacity ramps.
- Provide a fast, low-friction path to rollback or mitigate with clear triggers.
- Produce a concise, customer-ready release notes summary plus internal telemetry tasks.

Scope and when to use:
- Releases that change routing, batching heuristics, quantization profiles, or regional capacity behaviors.
- Not for data model/schema migrations or multi-day DB migrations (separate playbook).

Roles:
- Release Lead: Priya Malhotra (overall go/no-go).
- Canary Shepherd: Ethan Ruiz (observability & gating).
- Traffic Engineer: Liang Zhao (ramp scripts, rate-limiting).
- Incident Liaison: Maya Chen (pager and comms).
- Customer Success Liaison: Samira Khan (customer comms & targeted notifications).

Pre-deploy checklist (T-minus 48–2 hours):
- Confirm build artifact id and immutable release tag. (artifact: rld-2026-06-20-1423)
- Smoke tests green in staging for baseline latency P50/P95/P99.
- Load runner scenario created for prefix-KV cache warmup.
- Telemetry hooks validated: per-route token counts, error types, downstream latencies.
- Canary config prepared: percent slices, region list, TTL for ramp steps.
- Rollback artifact ready and verified: previous serving pool image and routing weights.
- Ops channel pinned and escalation roster notified (Slack #release-ops, Pager duty runbook).

Deploy day timeline (T0 is canary start):
- T-60m: Final sync with Release Lead, confirm obs dashboards open and pinned.
- T-30m: Freeze non-essential merges and hold deployments to dependent services.
- T0: Enable 1% traffic to canary cohort in region A (segment: internal+beta customers).
- T+7m: Quick health probe: request success rate, error-type distribution, downstream 500s.
- T+15m: If no regressions, increase to 5% traffic. Run synthetic burst test for 60s.
- T+45m: If stable, increase to 20% and start aftershock-sampling (see below).
- T+90m: Ramp to 50% if stability gates met; coordinate customer-targeted enabling.
- T+4h: Full regional ramp to 100% for region A if all gates remain green.

Gating criteria (pass/fail thresholds):
- Success rate: >= 99.7% over 10m windows for relevant endpoints.
- Relative error increase: < 0.15% absolute and < 20% relative vs baseline for P95 calls.
- Latency: P95 latency change < +20% and P99 < +25% compared to baseline.
- Token-cost delta: per-token compute cost change < +10% unless expected/approved.
- Resource saturation: GPU util < 85% sustained; memory pressure < 80% sustained.
- Alert storm detection: no more than 3 distinct new alert signatures within 30m.

Immediate abort triggers (rollback if any true):
- Any sustained >1% absolute increase in 500-class errors.
- Dependent service timeouts spiking >2x baseline for 15m.
- Telemetry gap: missing KV-cache hit metrics or missing tracing spans for 10m.
- Rapidly rising customer-facing incidents with P1 designation.

Aftershock sampling plan (unique section):
Definition: Aftershock sampling is an active short-window sampling of diverse user cohorts and synthetic traffic to detect low-probability failure modes that only appear after nontrivial traffic mixes.
- Sampling windows: 5–15 minute micro-windows executed at T+45m, T+3h, T+12h, and day+1.
- Cohorts: 1) Internal beta users (highly instrumented) 2) New-session users (cold-starts) 3) High concurrency bots (edge-case headers) 4) External customers on older SDKs.
- Method: Create small targeted routing slices (1–3% each, overlapping allowed) and run focused synthetic sequences that exercise cache eviction, long-prompt KV buildup, tool-calling code paths.
- Observables to capture per-window: per-route error types, token generation aborts, KV-hit ratio drift, trace end-to-end time, OOM/eviction logs.
- Escalation: Canary Shepherd reviews after each window; if any cohort fails gating, rollback that cohort to previous variant and hold other ramps.

Rollback checklist (1-click sequence where possible):
- Re-route traffic weights back to previous pool.
- Deploy previous image to canary nodes if infra image changed.
- Invalidate new config toggles in feature-flag store.
- Run immediate remediation smoke: 30s synthetic sanity in each affected region.
- Open incident doc with initial timeline and attach immediate rollback telemetry snapshots.

Post-deploy verification (72-hour matrix):
- Day 0 (first 6 hours): continuous 1m buckets for errors, 5m for latencies. Notify on any gate failure.
- Day 0–1: customer error reports triage twice per shift; CS liaison posts status.
- Day 1: run batch of load tests that replicate worst-case traffic patterns (long-run KV growth).
- Day 2: run degradations test (throttle downstream service mocks) to confirm graceful degradation.
- Day 3: finalize acceptance signoff and update release notes with any late-discovered mitigations.

Observability runbook (dashboards & query examples):
- Dashboards to pin: per-route latency (P50/P95/P99), error-class heatmap, per-host GPU/mem, KV-cache hit ratio, token-cost trend.
- Sample query: error-rate-by-route: sum(errors)/sum(requests) grouped by route over 10m.
- Tracing: locate a failing trace by correlating request id -> trace id; check KV span durations.

Release notes draft (customer-facing snippet):
Title: June 2026 routing & batching improvements (gradual rollout)
Summary: This release introduces routing fixes and batching optimizations to reduce tail latency during multi-tenant bursts. The rollout is staged by region and will be enabled gradually over the coming 72 hours.
What changed:
- Improved routing heuristics for fewer cold-start cache misses.
- Batching micro-optimizations that reduce CPU overhead at high concurrency.
- New configuration to allow safer per-route quantization profiles.
Impact & mitigations:
- Expected: small reductions in P95 latency for bursty traffic; no change to model outputs.
- Known risk: transient 502 spikes for a narrow class of long-running tool-invocation requests; we have a rollback plan and are monitoring closely.
- If you see issues: contact support@redwood.ai with subject line "June-2026-rollout"; include request ids and region.

Internal release notes items (to paste into internal digest):
- Release tag: rld-2026-06-20-1423
- Regions staged: us-west1 (A) -> eu-west1 (B) -> ap-south1 (C)
- Canary cohorts: internal beta + 1% of prod traffic initially
- Key telemetry dashboards: link:confluence/rls/dashboards/aftershock-2026

Four-week rollout calendar (compact):
- Week 0: branch, CI validation, staging perf tests, create canary config.
- Week 1 (release week): execute staged rollout with aftershock sampling and monitor 72h verification.
- Week 2: collect ops notes, small bugfix follow-up if needed, prepare patch release.
- Week 3: debrief, update runbook with lessons learned and add new synthetic scenarios.

Communications templates (short):
Internal Slack post (ops): "Rolling rld-2026-06-20-1423 -> starting canary us-west1 T0. Pin dashboards: aftershock-2026. Priya lead, Ethan shepherd. Any anomalies -> pager."
Customer email snippet: "We are rolling an optimization to improve latency; currently staged in us-west1 and will be enabled for you gradually. If you see unexpected behavior, reply to this thread or open a support ticket. ID: rld-2026-06-20-1423."

Open questions & follow-ups (capture during ops):
- Do we need an automated 'aftershock sampler' job to replace manual micro-windows? (owner: Traffic Engineer)
- Should we add a heatmap of cohort overlap to detect emergent combinatorial issues? (owner: Observability)
- Collect a sampling of failing traces to seed a regression test set.

Appendix: quick commands
- Rollback traffic weight: ./tools/trafficctl set-weight --release rld-2026-06-20-1423 --to previous
- Force canary pause: /ops/pause-canary --region us-west1
- Query for KV drift (example): prometheus query: (sum(kv_cache_hits) by(route) / sum(kv_cache_lookups) by(route))

Notes: keep this doc near the release calendar and attach postmortem templates after completion. This is intentionally compact so on-call can action quickly; expand to full runbook if release complexity increases.
